mechanism: Competitive inhibition of platelet COX-1; additive gastric mucosal irritation.
plain_language: Taking aspirin and ibuprofen together can significantly increase the risk of stomach irritation and gastrointestinal bleeding. Ibuprofen can also reduce the blood-thinning, heart-protective benefit of low-dose aspirin.
source: Local curated prototype dataset (Referenced: FDA Drug Safety Communication / BNF 84)

mechanism: Combined vitamin K antagonist anticoagulation and irreversible platelet COX-1 inhibition.
plain_language: Both medicines thin the blood through different pathways. Taking them together greatly increases the risk of severe or uncontrollable internal bleeding.
source: Local curated prototype dataset (Referenced: BNF 84 / Stockley's Drug Interactions)

mechanism: Synergistic enhancement of cyclic GMP-mediated vascular smooth muscle relaxation.
plain_language: Combining these medicines can cause a sudden, severe, and potentially life-threatening drop in blood pressure. They should never be taken together.
source: Local curated prototype dataset (Referenced: FDA Package Insert / AHA Guidelines)

mechanism: Nitrate-mediated cyclic GMP augmentation compounded by PDE-5 inhibition.
plain_language: Combining erectile dysfunction medication with nitrate heart medicines can cause an extreme, life-threatening drop in blood pressure.
source: Local curated prototype dataset (Referenced: FDA Package Insert / AHA Guidelines)

mechanism: Additive potassium retention via ACE inhibition and aldosterone antagonism.
plain_language: Both medicines can cause potassium to build up in your blood. High potassium levels (hyperkalemia) can lead to serious heart rhythm problems.
source: Local curated prototype dataset (Referenced: BNF 84 / Stockley's Drug Interactions)

mechanism: Potent inhibition of CYP3A4 metabolism by clarithromycin, markedly increasing atorvastatin plasma exposure.
plain_language: Clarithromycin slows down how your body breaks down atorvastatin, causing statin levels to rise dangerously. This increases the risk of severe muscle breakdown and kidney injury.
source: Local curated prototype dataset (Referenced: FDA Drug Safety Communication / Stockley's Drug Interactions)

mechanism: Additive serotonin reuptake inhibition increasing central synaptic serotonin concentrations.
plain_language: Taking sertraline with tramadol can lead to dangerously high serotonin levels in the brain (serotonin syndrome), causing confusion, tremors, fever, and rapid heart rate.
source: Local curated prototype dataset (Referenced: FDA MedWatch / BNF 84)

mechanism: NSAID reduces renal prostaglandin synthesis, impairing renal clearance of methotrexate.
plain_language: Naproxen can prevent your kidneys from clearing methotrexate, leading to elevated toxic levels that may suppress bone marrow function and damage blood cells.
source: Local curated prototype dataset (Referenced: BNF 84 / Stockley's Drug Interactions)

mechanism: Alcohol inhibits hepatic lactate gluconeogenesis, potentiating metformin-induced lactic acidosis.
plain_language: Consuming alcohol while on metformin substantially increases the risk of lactic acidosis, a rare but potentially dangerous buildup of acid in the bloodstream.
source: Local curated prototype dataset (Referenced: FDA Package Insert / BNF 84)

mechanism: Chelation of fluoroquinolone with multivalent cations (aluminum/magnesium) preventing intestinal absorption.
plain_language: Antacids containing aluminum or magnesium bind to ciprofloxacin in the stomach, preventing the antibiotic from being absorbed into your body and rendering it ineffective against infections.
source: Local curated prototype dataset (Referenced: BNF 84 / Stockley's Drug Interactions)

mechanism: Additive anticoagulant/antiplatelet effect and NSAID-induced gastric mucosal erosion.
plain_language: Ibuprofen irritates the stomach lining and impairs platelets, which drastically elevates the risk of major gastrointestinal bleeding when combined with warfarin.
source: Local curated prototype dataset (Referenced: BNF 84 / Stockley's Drug Interactions)

mechanism: P-glycoprotein inhibition by clarithromycin increases oral bioavailability and reduces renal excretion of digoxin.
plain_language: Clarithromycin can cause digoxin levels in the blood to double, leading to digitalis toxicity which may cause nausea, vision changes, and dangerous cardiac arrhythmias.
source: Local curated prototype dataset (Referenced: Stockley's Drug Interactions / BNF 84)

mechanism: Mild CYP3A4 inhibition by amlodipine increases simvastatin peak concentration and AUC.
plain_language: Amlodipine increases blood levels of simvastatin, which elevates the risk of muscle ache, weakness, and potential muscle breakdown (myopathy).
source: Local curated prototype dataset (Referenced: FDA Drug Safety Communication / BNF 84)

mechanism: Possible inhibition of vitamin K-dependent clotting factor synthesis by paracetamol metabolite with regular high-dose intake.
plain_language: Frequent or high-dose paracetamol taken regularly over multiple days can enhance the blood-thinning effect of warfarin and increase bleeding risk. Occasional single doses are usually lower risk.
source: Local curated prototype dataset (Referenced: BNF 84 / Stockley's Drug Interactions)

mechanism: Potent CYP2C9 inhibition by fluconazole impairs clearance of the active S-enantiomer of warfarin.
plain_language: Fluconazole blocks the breakdown of warfarin, causing blood-thinning levels to surge and creating a very high risk of bruising and severe hemorrhage.
source: Local curated prototype dataset (Referenced: BNF 84 / FDA Package Insert)

mechanism: CYP2D6 inhibition and synergistic serotonin uptake blockade.
plain_language: Combining fluoxetine and tramadol increases the risk of seizures and serotonin syndrome, while also reducing the pain-relieving effect of tramadol.
source: Local curated prototype dataset (Referenced: Stockley's Drug Interactions / BNF 84)

mechanism: Competitive CYP2C19 inhibition prevents biotransformation of clopidogrel to its active antiplatelet metabolite.
plain_language: Omeprazole may reduce the effectiveness of clopidogrel at preventing blood clots, potentially increasing the risk of heart attack or stroke in cardiac patients.
source: Local curated prototype dataset (Referenced: FDA Safety Warning / BNF 84)

mechanism: Disulfiram-like inhibition of acetaldehyde dehydrogenase causing accumulation of acetaldehyde.
plain_language: Drinking alcohol while taking metronidazole can cause severe facial flushing, throbbing headache, nausea, vomiting, sweating, and rapid heartbeat.
source: Local curated prototype dataset (Referenced: BNF 84 / FDA Package Insert)

mechanism: Antagonism between beta-2 agonist bronchodilator and non-selective beta-blocker.
plain_language: Propranolol blocks the airways and counteracts albuterol, which can trigger severe asthma attacks or life-threatening bronchospasm in patients with respiratory conditions.
source: Local curated prototype dataset (Referenced: BNF 84 / Stockley's Drug Interactions)

mechanism: Additive prolongation of cardiac ventricular repolarization (QT interval).
plain_language: Both medicines can affect the electrical rhythm of the heart. Taking them together significantly increases the risk of dangerous irregular heartbeats (Torsades de pointes).
source: Local curated prototype dataset (Referenced: FDA Drug Safety Communication / BNF 84)

mechanism: Inhibition of CYP1A2 and alteration of gut flora synthesis of vitamin K.
plain_language: Ciprofloxacin can markedly enhance the anticoagulant effect of warfarin, resulting in elevated INR readings and dangerous bleeding episodes.
source: Local curated prototype dataset (Referenced: BNF 84 / Stockley's Drug Interactions)

mechanism: Exogenous potassium supplementation in presence of potassium-sparing diuretic.
plain_language: Taking potassium supplements while on spironolactone can cause blood potassium levels to rise dangerously high, creating a risk of fatal heart arrhythmias.
source: Local curated prototype dataset (Referenced: BNF 84 / FDA Package Insert)

mechanism: Additive ulcerogenic effect on gastrointestinal mucosa.
plain_language: Taking NSAIDs like ibuprofen together with corticosteroids like prednisolone dramatically increases the likelihood of stomach ulcers and serious internal bleeding.
source: Local curated prototype dataset (Referenced: BNF 84 / Stockley's Drug Interactions)

mechanism: Additive cyclooxygenase inhibition with heightened gastrointestinal ulceration risk.
plain_language: Taking two NSAID pain relievers together increases the risk of stomach ulcers and kidney strain without providing additional pain relief.
source: Local curated prototype dataset (Referenced: BNF 84 / Stockley's Drug Interactions)

mechanism: Inhibition of CYP2C9 metabolism by fluconazole decreases phenytoin clearance.
plain_language: Fluconazole causes phenytoin to accumulate in the bloodstream, increasing the likelihood of toxicity symptoms such as ataxia, dizziness, confusion, and nystagmus.
source: Local curated prototype dataset (Referenced: Stockley's Drug Interactions / BNF 84)
